claims.assertion: The GPS record shows one off-route segment, 18:50–19:00, in which 6.93 km were driven where the optimal route covers 2.84 km, adding 4.09 km and reaching up to 884 m from the optimal route; this is an unexempted detour under RD-1.

The trip as a whole ran 24.4 km against an optimal 19.8 km (+4.6 km, +23%) and 39.8 min against an estimated 28.3 min, so the deviation entered the metered fare, which on RydeTAXI is charged per distance/time unit.

The driver proposed the named road Defu Avenue 1 at 18:46 and the rider replied 'Can lah, go ahead.' at 18:47, i.e. before the segment began at 18:50, so the rider's own message is a consent (not merely the driver's later statement at F11).

However, the consent reaches only driving on Defu Avenue 1: no fact in the record names any road driven during the 18:50–19:00 segment or otherwise ties that segment to Defu Avenue 1, and the segment ran up to 884 m from the optimal route — the tie required by RD-5 for a named-road consent is absent, so this element is undetermined (G13).

The driver's written claim that he asked before turning off via Defu Avenue 1 is only a post-trip statement (F11) and cannot by itself establish either consent or that the driven segment was in fact Defu Avenue 1.

No traffic incident is recorded near the route during the trip window, so the driver's congestion justification is not supported by an incident fact and cannot be exempted under RD-4(a); the only congestion record, KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY at speed band 2 from 18:24–18:50, is relevant only because that expressway was on the optimal route the driver departed from at 18:50.
A speed-band record alone does not exempt the segment under RD-4(b), because band ≤ 2 is only corroborative and MVP does not exempt on a band alone.

The billed excess distance was 4.54 km at $1.4100/km = $6.40 (F4), the per-km rate being this trip's distance fare $34.39 / 24.39 km (F7), so the metered overcharge attributable to the route is computable.
The waiting fee billed was only $0.11 for 0.4 min, consistent with the metered waiting unit rather than a fixed non-metered charge, and it is not part of the disputed overcharge.

The driver's record shows 1 upheld dispute in the last 90 days, which with this established route violation makes the case 'repeated' and supports an account flag; profile facts are used only for this additional action, not to prove the detour.

weaknesses: The rider did send an own consent message before the segment (F9 'Can lah, go ahead.' in reply to F8's Defu Avenue 1 proposal), so the driver will argue the segment is fully exempt under RD-5; our answer rests on the absence of any record tying the driven segment to Defu Avenue 1 (F3 shows only distance/geometry, no road names), which the judge may read as enough consent for the whole diversion rather than as undetermined.

There is real congestion evidence on the optimal corridor: F12 records the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 18:24–18:50, which the driver will cite under RD-4(b) even though RD-4(b) alone does not exempt in the MVP and no incident fact exists (F15).

The billed excess (F4: 4.54 km, $6.40) is larger than the GPS segment excess (F3: 4.09 km); RD-2 refuses refund of the difference outside unexempted segments, and if the segment is found consented or undetermined the refund falls to zero or the case is sent to a human.

F1's +4.6 km optimum-vs-actual gap includes normal meter/route-corridor variance (F2 shows only +11.5 min), so the driver may argue part of the excess is map-matching noise rather than detour mileage.

The rider will point to the fare: $50.12 charged (F7) including $6.40 of excess distance billed (F4), well above the app's quoted trip, which supports a refund claim under RD-2 if the segment is held unexempted, and the rider's complaint expressly questions whether the road driven was the road agreed.

The driver's only corroboration for the agreed road is his own after-the-fact written statement (F11), which under G11/G13 carries little weight against the absence of any record naming the road driven; the traffic band evidence (F12) explains the reason offered but does not prove which road was taken.

points.response: Accepted as far as it goes: F3 is the only off-route segment, adding 4.09 km, and my refund is built on that segment alone — not on the whole +4.6 km trip excess of F1 — because RD-2 refuses the corridor/matching residue.

Conceded on consent existing and on timing: the rider's own message F9 ('Can lah, go ahead.') was sent at 18:47, before the F3 segment start at 18:50, in reply to the named road 'Defu Avenue 1' in F8, and the chat record is complete and timestamped (F10). Consent therefore exists — but RD-5 makes a named-road consent cover only driving on that road, and D2 cites nothing that ties the driven segment to Defu Avenue 1.

F12 does not exempt the segment: it is a traffic band, and RD-4(b) says a band alone is corroborative only and is not a stand-alone exemption in this system, while RD-4(a) requires an incident fact on the replaced stretch, and F15 records no incident near the route.

The arithmetic in D5 is mine (4.09 km × $1.4100/km = $5.77, rate from F4/F7); the only disagreement is the exemption, and since the only consent is a named-road consent with no record tying the segment to that road, the segment is undetermined/unexempted and the $5.77 stands.
No dispute on the waiting unit: my brief already states the $0.11 waiting fee (F5) is not part of the refund claim, so this point is agreed and reduces nothing.

Agreed that no incident exists and the driver need not prove a blockage, but the same facts cut against the driver: F15 shows no incident on the optimal route, so nothing in the record explains why the alternative had to be 6.93 km where the optimal covers 2.84 km (F3), which is the excess the rider was metered for.
The rider does not press SAFE-1/SAFE-2 and I do not seek escalation: nothing in F8–F11 is a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation.
Withdrawn: F18 shows route: 0 upheld in the 90-day window, so RD-6's condition route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is not met and I no longer request a flag_account — my C10 is withdrawn.

Conceded that F3 is a single off-route segment adding 4.09 km; but RD-1 only makes a segment 'unexempted' after RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 review, and here a rider-authored message predating the segment (F9 at 18:47, before the 18:50 start in F3) sits in the record.

Correct that the meter carried the kilometres (F7, F1, F2); but RD-2 refunds only the distance units of segments not exempted, so the whole-trip +23% figure does nothing once the single segment is consented to under RD-5, and the difference between F4's 4.54 km and F3's 4.09 km is expressly not refundable anyway.

We adopt C3: F9 'Can lah, go ahead.' is a rider-authored consent sent at 18:47, before the segment start at 18:50 (F3), in direct reply to the driver's named proposal at F8, and the chat record is complete and timestamped (F10).

Conceded in part: F3 carries no road name, so no fact ties the driven 6.93 km to Defu Avenue 1; but nothing places it elsewhere either, so on this record the tie is undetermined rather than disproved, and under G13 that sends the segment to a human rather than automatically refunding it.
We do not rest the case on F11; F11 is merely consistent with the pre-emptive messages at F8-F9, and we accept it cannot prove by itself which road was driven.

We do not claim an RD-4 exemption: F15 shows no incident, and we rely on the rider's own consent under RD-5, with F12 (Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, band 2, 10-19 km/h, 18:24-18:50) used only to explain why a reasonable driver would propose the alternative at 18:46 (F8).
Conceded: F12 alone cannot exempt the segment under RD-4(b) in the MVP, which is why our exemption argument is RD-5, not RD-4.

The $1.41/km rate is correct (F4, F7), but arithmetic on it does not create entitlement: RD-2's refund is the sum of unexempted segments' extra_km times rate, and with the only segment consented (F9) or at most undetermined (F3) the refundable distance is zero, not 4.09 km, and certainly not 4.54 km, which includes mileage RD-2 excludes.
Agreed that the $0.11 for 0.4 min (F5, F7) is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and is chargeable as recorded under RD-3(c); it is not part of the dispute.

There is one upheld dispute in 90 days (F18) but both category counters read 0 (route: 0, no-show: 0), so no route violation is 'established' here; RD-6 requires a finding under RD-2 or RD-1 before any flag, and profile facts may never carry the underlying finding.
